clue.text: Good supporter and hard worker

parts.note: a rafter is a beam supporting a roof

explanation.surface: Praise for someone who backs a cause and toils hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A grafter, in British slang, is someone who works diligently and tirelessly.

clue.text: Understand snap?

definitions.meaning: to grasp the situation or comprehend it
read literally, to obtain a photograph, as when taking a snapshot

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to grasp what is going on, and literally to acquire an image such as a photo.

clue.text: A connection is cut

parts.note: a bridge connects two places

explanation.surface: A link has been severed.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten it, i.e. to cut it down.

clue.text: On the spot in further education

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'On the spot in further education' (5) for THERE: 'On the spot' can define THERE, but no standard reading of 'in further education' supplies wordplay for it, and no source gives the parse.
annotationWithheld.clue: On the spot in further education

clue.text: A woman's not so brutal

parts.note: Ruth is a woman's name; the 's stands for 'is', a link
less means not so much, to a smaller degree

explanation.surface: A certain woman is less harsh than she might be.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruthless means without pity or compassion, hence cruel and brutal.

clue.text: Rod's hairpiece

definitions.meaning: a thin flexible stick or cane
a tress of false hair added to one's own

explanation.surface: A man called Rod owns a wig.
explanation.definitionFit: A switch is both a slender flexible twig and a length of false hair worn as a hairpiece.

clue.text: Only fellow without a grave

parts.note: sole means only, single

indicators.note: without tells us to remove the letter A from the word for a fellow

parts.note: a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: The lone man who has no burial place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like a burial place, but it is the adjective meaning serious; 'without' takes A out of MAN, leaving MN.
explanation.definitionFit: Solemn and grave are synonyms meaning serious and dignified in manner.

clue.text: Cincinnus is ready with Rameau's last composition

parts.note: the setter Cincinnus, speaking of himself, says I'M
prompt means ready, quick to act

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: The setter is prepared to play the closing piece by the French composer Rameau.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by their pseudonym, so 'Cincinnus is' gives I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: An impromptu is a short piece of music, often for piano, in an improvised style.

clue.text: Church leader in Ireland not in favour of wine

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of the country's name

parts.note: anti means against, not in favour

explanation.surface: A senior Irish cleric disapproves of drinking wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church leader' looks like one phrase meaning a bishop; split it into CH and the indicator 'leader in' for the I of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany in Italy.

clue.text: Medicinal plant — one left after plague

indicators.note: after places the letters for one and left following the word for plague

parts.note: to plague someone is to torment them
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A herbal remedy was the only one remaining after an epidemic.
explanation.definitionFit: Tormentil is a small yellow-flowered plant whose root was used in herbal medicine as an astringent.

clue.text: Article seized by strait-laced old king

indicators.note: seized by means held inside, so the article goes within the word for strait-laced

parts.note: prim means prudish, strait-laced
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece confiscated by a prudish former monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Priam was the legendary king of Troy at the time of the Trojan War.

clue.text: Floundering, need mariner at sea

indicators.note: floundering means struggling clumsily, so the letters that follow are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A sailor struggling in the water needs help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' looks like a phrase meaning confused, but 'at' is anagram fodder and only 'sea' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean is the sea lying between southern Europe and North Africa.

clue.text: He would get time off to avoid commitment

parts.note: he would contracts to he'd

indicators.note: off means removed, so the abbreviation for time is taken away from the word get

explanation.surface: A man would take some leave to dodge his obligations.
explanation.definitionFit: To hedge is to avoid committing oneself, as in hedging one's bets.

clue.text: An old poem in translation made to look silly

indicators.note: translation turns words into a different form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ancient verse rendered into another language came out ridiculous.
explanation.definitionFit: To be lampooned is to be publicly mocked or satirised, made to appear ridiculous.

clue.text: Eccentric puts rice in baked pastry

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An oddball adds rice to a baked pastry case.
explanation.definitionFit: A piecrust is the baked pastry shell or covering of a pie.

clue.text: One whose relations are said to be entertaining

definitions.text: One whose relations are said to be entertaining

parts.words: One whose relations are said to be entertaining
parts.note: relations here are not relatives but things related, i.e. stories told, by a skilled teller

explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a person who tells anecdotes in an amusing and skilful way.

clue.text: Made a mess of sediment in river? Just the opposite

indicators.note: in signals that one piece is put inside the other
just the opposite reverses the stated arrangement, so the river goes inside the sediment instead

parts.note: silt is fine sediment deposited by water
the Po is the longest river in Italy

explanation.surface: Was sediment in a river ruined, or vice versa?
explanation.definitionFit: Spoilt means ruined, so to have spoilt something is to have made a mess of it.

clue.text: Production plan in coarse form

indicators.note: form is read as a verb, shape, so the letters are moulded into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A rough outline of a manufacturing plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a link: it is part of the fodder with 'coarse'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is the outline plot of a film or play, the plan for a production.

clue.text: Copper in front of indecent junior minister's office

indicators.note: in front of places the symbol before the word for indecent

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
racy means risqué, slightly indecent

explanation.surface: A policeman confronts a sleazy junior government minister in his office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer; here it is the metal. 'Minister' is a clergyman, not a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A curacy is the post of a curate, a junior member of the clergy assisting a parish priest.

clue.text: Judges playing conkers

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moved about as in a game

explanation.surface: Referees at a game of conkers, the British children's game of swinging horse chestnuts on strings.
explanation.definitionFit: To reckon is to judge or estimate, so reckons is a synonym for judges.

clue.text: Military vehicle for which one should be prepared?

definitions.meaning: an armoured car used for reconnaissance

definitions.text: for which one should be prepared?
definitions.meaning: read whimsically as a car for a Boy Scout, whose motto is Be Prepared

explanation.surface: An army vehicle that one ought to be ready for.
explanation.definitionFit: A scout car is a fast, lightly armoured military vehicle for reconnaissance.

clue.text: In Islamabad I may be excellent

definitions.meaning: the letter I starting the word Islamabad is an upper-case letter; Islamabad itself is Pakistan's seat of government

explanation.surface: Someone imagines living in Pakistan's chief city would be splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital means an upper-case letter or a seat of government, and is also dated slang for excellent.

clue.text: Autocrat has first of shocks in store

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside the word for store

parts.note: a depot is a storehouse

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A tyrant has some surprises waiting for us.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is a ruler with absolute power, an autocrat.

clue.text: Lack of interest in a Parisian business

parts.note: un is French for a, as a Parisian would say it
a concern is a business or firm

explanation.surface: A French company shows no interest.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconcern is indifference, a lack of interest or worry.

clue.text: Beginner in Athens

parts.note: not a novice in Greece but the character that opens the Greek letter sequence, before beta

explanation.definitionFit: It is the first character in the Greek script, so it begins the letter sequence used in Athens.

clue.text: A mostly dreary time — but not for children

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter of the word for dreary is dropped

parts.note: dull means dreary

explanation.surface: A rather dull spell, though not one meant for kids.
explanation.definitionFit: Adult content is material deemed unsuitable for children.

clue.text: Awake memories of one who raised Cain accepting fine

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the word for fine goes inside the name

parts.note: in Genesis Eve was the mother of Cain, so she raised him
OK means fine, all right

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up recollections of a troublemaker who welcomed a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised Cain' looks like the idiom for causing trouble; here it is literal, the mother who brought up Cain.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to call up or awaken memories or feelings.

clue.text: Twirl rake in deep hole next to hollow tree

indicators.note: next to puts the remaining piece alongside, at the end
in places the libertine inside the deep hole

parts.note: a pit is a deep hole
a roué is a rake, a debauched man

indicators.note: hollow means emptied out, leaving only the outside letters

explanation.surface: Garden tool spins in a pit by a hollow trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rake' suggests the garden tool; here it is a dissolute man. Hollowing TREE leaves TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirouette is a spin on one foot, as in ballet, a twirl.

clue.text: Liveliness of priest after conversion

indicators.note: conversion means changing form, so the letters of priest are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clergyman shows new spirit once converted.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is French-derived for spirit and liveliness of mind.

clue.text: Flier from Dartmoor to Lancashire

indicators.note: from indicates the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A bird travels from a Devon moor up to a northern county.
explanation.definitionFit: The ortolan is a small European bunting, a bird and so a flier.
